channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: TSE discutirá em plenário decisão de Mendonça que mandou governo informar gastos com publicidade
item.description: The TSE will discuss in plenary the decision by Minister André Mendonça requiring the Lula government to disclose public advertising spending from 2023 to 2026, after a highlight request voided the virtual vote. The PL-led action alleges excessive institutional advertising spending in the first half of 2026, potentially violating Brazil's Election Law (Art. 73, VII, Law 9.504/1997). Court President Kassio Nunes Marques will set the date for the in-person session.

item.title: Advogado de Carla Zambelli quer ação para investigar Lulinha
item.description: Fabio Pagnozzi, lawyer for ex-deputy Carla Zambelli, announced he will request the Spanish Public Prosecutor's Office to investigate Synapta SL, the company of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), eldest son of President Lula. Pagnozzi claims he verified the company's Madrid address is a fiscal address with no real activity, suspecting a shell company and questioning who funds Lulinha in Spain.

item.title: Crusoé: Divirta-se com o plano de governo de Augusto Cury
item.description: Augusto Cury, candidate for the Avante party and known as the world's most-read psychiatrist, filed his government plan with the TSE. His candidacy is framed as an act of voluntarism aimed at healing others' suffering, emphasizing his international publishing reach across more than 90 countries. The piece highlights his emotional and symbolic appeal rather than concrete public policy proposals.

item.title: 'Liberdade de imprensa não está em questão no Brasil', diz Cármen Lúcia
item.description: STF Minister Carmen Lucia stated that press freedom is not in question in Brazil, emphasizing the constitutional guarantee of source confidentiality. She declined to comment on the specific case involving a police operation against a source linked to reports critical of Minister Flávio Dino, but said she will vote when the matter reaches the Supreme Court plenary. Her remarks were made during a BBC World Service and BBC News Brasil event on combating disinformation.

item.title: “Quem foi a liderança nacional mais recente? Eu e Bolsonaro”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated that he and former President Jair Bolsonaro are the only national leaders in the current political landscape, noting that Bolsonaro has support in every Brazilian state. The comment was made during an interview on the podcast 'Não Inviabilize'.

item.title: Grêmio lança 3º uniforme em homenagem aos 30 anos da tríplice coroa
item.description: Grêmio unveiled its third kit in honor of the 30th anniversary of the 1996 treble, which included the Gaúcho, Brasileirão, and Recopa Sul-Americana titles. The jersey will debut in the match against Chapecoense on August 30, valid for the 25th round of the Brazilian Championship. The launch event featured players from the men's, women's, and under-20 squads, as well as Dinho, who participated in the 1996 triumphs.

item.title: Lula questionou Lulinha sobre natureza da relação com lobista investigada no esquema do INSS, afirmam aliados
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reportedly questioned his son, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), about the nature of his friendship with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation in the INSS influence-peddling scheme. According to allies, Lula raised the concern in a phone call prior to former chief of staff Marco Aurélio Ribeiro Santana being targeted, saying the relationship seemed 'strange' given his presidential status. Lulinha reportedly explained that Luchsinger has been a close friend of his wife for nearly ten years. Lula stated he had asked his son’s lawyers not to seek dismissal of the ongoing investigations.

item.title: Salário mínimo: governo projeta piso de R$ 1.741 em 2027
item.description: The Lula government has updated its projection for Brazil's 2027 minimum wage to R$1,741, up R$24 from the April estimate of R$1,717, reflecting revised inflation forecasts. This represents a 7.4% increase over the current R$1,621 minimum wage and will be included in the 2026 budget bill to be submitted to Congress on July 31. The adjustment will affect pensions, social benefits, unemployment insurance, and MEI contributions, as nearly 45% of RGPS benefits are tied to the minimum wage.

item.title: Patrus troca 1º debate em Minas por lançamento da campanha de Lula
item.description: Patrus Ananias (PT) announced he will not attend the first gubernatorial debate in Minas Gerais, scheduled for this Sunday (August 16) on Band Minas, because he will be in São Bernardo do Campo attending the launch of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s (PT) re-election campaign. He stated that the commitment with Lula was pre-arranged and he cannot return to Belo Horizonte in time for the debate, though he confirmed his presence in upcoming debates with other broadcasters.

item.title: Michelle estuda pedido ao STF para acompanhar estreia de Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro is considering requesting authorization from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to allow a trusted person to accompany former President Jair Bolsonaro during the first official campaign event of her son, Flávio Bolsonaro, for the presidency, scheduled for this Sunday in Copacabana. Her participation in the event depends on resolving the care situation for the former president, who is under judicial restrictions.

item.title: Com erro em registro, candidato do Agir declara ter R$ 1,5 quatrilhão
item.description: Tiago Társis, the Agir party's Senate candidate for the Federal District, had a typo in his asset declaration filed with the TSE, showing R$1.5 quadrillion instead of the correct R$15,000. He explained the error came from a website patent declaration and said the party will correct it. Társis stated he had tried to declare the accurate amount before the election to do the right thing.

item.title: Rogério Marinho reage a Kassab e diz que PSD atua para eleger Lula
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) criticized PSD national president Gilberto Kassab after Kassab stated that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) has no chance of winning the 2026 presidential election. Marinho accused the PSD of acting as an 'auxiliary line' for Lula's government, citing three PSD ministers in the federal cabinet and claiming Ronaldo Caiado's candidacy is not genuine. He argued the political system has united against Flávio Bolsonaro due to feeling threatened.

item.title: Jovem deixa rastros e assume que tentou filiar Lula ao Missão
item.description: A 16-year-old admitted attempting to register President Lula with the far-right Missão party to expose flaws in the TSE’s voter registration system, following a similar incident involving Flávio Bolsonaro. He provided his personal phone number, email containing his name and other identifiers, and used Lula’s official data, arguing the system is too vulnerable to impersonation. Missão canceled the registration before it was processed and filed a judicial complaint for ideological fraud.

item.title: Fernando Holiday diz que Missão 'cometeu crime' em filiação fraudulenta de Flávio Bolsonaro: 'Moleques irresponsáveis e burros'
item.description: Former councilman Fernando Holiday accused the Missão party of committing a crime by facilitating a fraudulent affiliation that blocked Flávio Bolsonaro from registering his presidential candidacy under the PL. He claims the party had knowledge of the issue since at least August 2, contradicting its claim of being caught off guard, and argues that its reaction is inconsistent with its own timeline.

item.title: Zema inicia campanha presidencial com missa em Montes Claros
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate for the Novo party, launched his official campaign in Montes Claros, Minas Gerais, with a mass at the Nossa Senhora da Conceição e São José parish. The choice of this city in northern Minas Gerais reflects an effort to expand his base beyond the Southeast, emphasizing his image as a technical and moderate manager. The event marked the symbolic start of his 2026 electoral journey.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: A seletividade processual do Direito Xandônico
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program analyzed the procedural selectivity of Minister Alexandre de Moraes in a case involving a Maranhão journalist who disclosed sensitive information about Minister Flávio Dino. It also discussed the start of the 2026 electoral campaign, highlighting the registration of Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy.

item.title: Parlamentares defendem rigor penal no plano de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Allied lawmakers of Flávio Bolsonaro advocate for stricter penal legislation as a priority in their public security plan, including prison system expansion and measures against criminal organizations. The proposal aligns with Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) government plan, which centers on hardline penal policies as a core campaign pillar.

item.title: Integrantes do governo não acreditam que reciprocidade contra os EUA seja aplicada antes da eleição
item.description: Lula’s government officials believe effective reciprocity against U.S. tariffs will not be applied before the October elections, as the process takes 60–90 days. They prefer alternatives like suspending U.S. intellectual property royalties over direct taxation to avoid harming Brazil’s economy. They also expect the U.S. to only resume negotiations after the election, with differing expectations depending on whether Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro wins.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos que mais arrecadaram em vaquinhas para as eleições de 2026? Veja ranking
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) leads the 2026 electoral crowdfunding ranking with R$1.23 million raised, followed by Marcel van Hattem (Novo) and Jones Manoel (PSOL). The three candidates together have raised approximately R$2.5 million through TSE-homologated crowdfunding platforms, indicating growing digital supporter engagement.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral começa neste domingo; conheça as regras
item.description: Electoral campaigning for the 2026 elections officially begins this Sunday (16), allowing candidates to directly solicit votes, hold rallies, and conduct live internet broadcasts. Free radio and TV advertising starts on August 28, with 70 minutes daily allocated for 30- and 60-second spots. The TSE has established strict rules to ensure fairness and prevent abuses, banning deepfakes, audio/video manipulation, and requiring accountability for false, hateful, or antidemocratic content, while regulating AI use and social media in campaigns.

item.title: Alfredo Gaspar, vice de Flávio, declara R$ 565 mil de patrimônio
item.description: Alfredo Gaspar, running mate of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the 2026 presidential ticket, declared R$ 564,666.16 in assets to the TSE in 2026, reflecting a real growth of 63.49% compared to his 2022 declaration, adjusted for inflation. His largest assets include a 2024 Jeep Compass (R$ 158,170.42), a house in Marechal Deodoro/AL (R$ 95,900.00), and a stake in a fuel station (R$ 27,345.31).

item.title: “Entramos com a Lei de Reciprocidade para mostrar que a gente não é pouca coisa”
item.description: President Lula announced the initiation of a reciprocity process with the United States in response to tariffs imposed on Brazilian imports, stating the move is meant to show that Brazil 'is not insignificant'. The government had already notified the White House on Thursday, the 13th, and Lula emphasized that while he wants to maintain good relations with the U.S., he will not yield on defending national interests.

item.title: Ex-ator da Globo declara R$ 3,6 mi e concorre a deputado
item.description: Former Globo actor Humberto Martins declared R$ 3.6 million in assets to the TSE and is running for federal deputy from Rio de Janeiro in 2026 under the DC party. His largest holdings are in life insurance and pension plans (R$ 2.1 million), followed by an apartment (R$ 600 thousand) and financial investments. He also declared R$ 130 thousand in an overseas bank account, a plot of land in Campo Paulista (SP), and a motorcycle.

item.title: Após desastroso enredo sobre Lula, escola de samba mira em santa das causas impossíveis
item.description: After a controversial 2026 parade featuring a politically charged samba-enredo about Lula that led to their relegation from the Special Group, Acadêmicos de Niterói aims for a comeback in the Série Ouro with a religious theme. Their new enredo, 'A Rosa do Impossível', honors Saint Rita of Cascia, patron saint of impossible causes, focusing on her life, faith, and suffering. Carnival designer Tiago Martins returns, seeking to move away from political polarization and embrace spiritual redemption.

item.title: Rogério Marinho rebate Kassab e diz que candidatura de Caiado ‘não é para valer’
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) rebutted PSD president Gilberto Kassab, claiming Ronaldo Caiado's (PSD) candidacy 'is not for real', accusing the PSD of supporting Lula and acting as an auxiliary line for the PT government. Marinho said the system united because it feels threatened by Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy. The statement comes amid competition for the center-right electorate between the campaigns of Flávio Bolsonaro and Ronaldo Caiado.

item.title: MP Eleitoral dá 5 dias para gestão Tarcísio explicar relato de ação da PM contra motorista de Haddad
item.description: The Electoral Public Prosecutor’s Office has given Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’s administration five days to explain an alleged operation by military police that reportedly followed and confronted the driver of opposition candidate Fernando Haddad after he left his residence, in a possible misuse of state apparatus for political intimidation. The MPE is investigating whether this constitutes abuse of power and prohibited conduct, requesting documents from the Public Security Secretariat, the PM, and hotel security footage, while also forwarding the case to the São Paulo MP for potential criminal analysis.

item.title: Renan Santos denuncia ameaça de morte em ato de início de campanha
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) reported receiving a death threat via the 'Leftypol' forum, allegedly from a USP law student who claimed to be armed and planning to attack him at the campaign kickoff event in Largo São Francisco on Sunday (16). The candidate's team forwarded the threat to authorities and confirmed the event will proceed as planned with enhanced security measures. A protest by USP's XI de Agosto Academic Center was held on Thursday (13) against the event's location.

item.title: Lula minimiza vantagem de Ciro no Datafolha e diz ser 'quase impossível' Elmano perder com apoio dele no Ceará
item.description: Lula downplayed Ciro Gomes' lead in the Datafolha poll, which shows him 19 points ahead of Elmano de Freitas in the Ceará gubernatorial race, saying it would be 'almost humanly impossible' for Elmano to lose with his backing and that of Camilo Santana and Cid Gomes. He linked his own vote to Elmano’s and criticized Ciro as overly personalistic, stating 'the world revolves around him'.

item.title: Crusoé: Os candidatos que querem reformar o Judiciário
item.description: Presidential candidates have submitted their government plans to the TSE, with Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema standing out for including specific judicial reform proposals in their documents. Renan Santos, while mentioning the topic minimally in his formal plan, has previously discussed judicial reform in interviews, including a sabatina with O Antagonista.

item.title: Prêmio da Globo mingou: ex-BBB Matteus Amaral diz ao TSE ter poucos bens
item.description: Matteus Amaral, BBB 24 runner-up and União Brasil candidate for Rio Grande do Sul, told the TSE he owns assets worth R$ 73,000 — far below the prizes he won on the show, including cash, a car, and appliances. His declared assets include a land plot in Alegrete (R$ 66,000), company shares, fixed-income investments, and a bank balance. The report also notes controversy over his 2014 racial self-declaration for affirmative action admission at IFFar, which he denies making knowingly.

item.title: Bandeira de Lula contra tarifaço e pelo PIX, soberania é usada por equipe de Flávio para tratar de segurança pública
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) incorporated the concept of 'sovereignty' into his government program, using it 12 times to address public security as a counter-narrative to Lula’s discourse. His team believes the term resonates with voter concerns about urban violence and aims to reframe the debate domestically, criticizing Nicolás Maduro’s visit to Brazil and advocating closer ties with the U.S., Israel, and Argentina.

item.title: As duas mudanças que André Mendonça defende para o STF
item.description: Minister André Mendonça proposes two changes for the STF: ending its role as the initial instance for criminal investigations — suggesting they be handled by lower courts like the STJ — and limiting who can file constitutional actions, requiring a minimum partisan composition instead of allowing any party with a single representative or small association to do so. He argues the STF should focus on reviewing decisions via habeas corpus and appeals, not on initiating criminal probes.

item.title: Flávio e Marinho rebatem Kassab e dizem que PSD atua para eleger Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and his campaign coordinator, Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), criticized PSD leader Gilberto Kassab after he said the PL candidate has 'zero chance' of winning the 2026 election. They accused the PSD of acting as an 'auxiliary line' for Lula’s government, claiming Ronaldo Caiado’s (PSD) candidacy is a sham to help Lula win. Marinho said masks are falling and that Flávio will win to restore prosperity, while Flávio declared 'PSD is Lula' and that everyone is against Brazil.

item.title: Kassab diz que centrão está com Lula e vê 'chance zero' de Flávio se eleger
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, the vice-presidential candidate on Ronaldo Caiado's (PSD) ticket, stated that the centrão parties are supporting Lula's (PT) re-election and that Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) chance of winning the 2026 presidential race is 'zero'. The remarks were made at a business gathering in São Paulo.

item.title: Caiado declara patrimônio de R$ 52,56 milhões, com imóveis rurais e rebanho
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD presidential candidate and former governor of Goiás, declared assets worth R$ 52.56 million in 2026, with rural properties (R$ 36.21 million) and livestock (R$ 10.49 million) making up nearly 90% of the total. His wealth grew 111.29% since 2022, when he declared R$ 27.68 million (adjusted to R$ 25.21 million for inflation). He also holds R$ 4.29 million in tax-exempt fixed-income assets, minor equity stakes, and small amounts in bank deposits, vehicles, and capitalization bonds.

item.title: Lula não sabe nada sobre Lulinha?
item.description: President Lula (PT) reiterated his confidence in the innocence of his son, Fábio Luis Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, stating that he believes him despite three ongoing investigations. Lula emphasized that Lulinha 'swears by everything sacred that he has nothing' to be blamed for, reaffirming his familial support even amid the accusations.

item.title: MPF instaura inquérito para apurar caso do motorista de Haddad seguido por viatura da PM de SP
item.description: The Federal Public Prosecutor's Office (MPF) opened an investigation into alleged police intimidation of Fernando Haddad's driver following a televised debate, with claims of institutional retaliation for his criticism of state security policies. The 'Desperta SP' coalition filed a formal complaint highlighting a temporal link between Haddad's public remarks and the incident, requesting operational documents from the Military Police and the state security secretary. The government stated the patrol was searching for a 'glass-breaking' gang, but Haddad disputes the timing and vehicle details.

item.title: OEA enviará missão internacional para acompanhar eleições no Brasil
item.description: The Organization of American States (OEA) will deploy an international mission to monitor Brazil's general elections in October 2026, marking the fifth time the organization has observed elections in the country since 2018. Observers will visit polling stations and meet with Brazilian authorities during both rounds of voting, following an agreement signed by OAB Secretary-General Albert Ramdim and Brazil's OEA representative Benoni Belli. In addition to the OEA, the EU, Mercosur Parliament (Parlasul), and the Inter-American Union of Electoral Bodies (Uniore) have also confirmed they will send observation missions.

item.title: Crise entre Milei e Lula ofusca apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro nas redes, diz pesquisa
item.description: Javier Milei's support for Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy lost traction in online discourse amid the escalating diplomatic crisis between the Argentine president and Lula. Datrix Digital's analysis of 3,990 social media posts from July 18 to August 11, 2026, found that the bilateral conflict overshadowed mentions of Milei's backing for the Bolsonaro-aligned candidate.

item.title: 2027, a hora da verdade
item.description: 2027 will be a moment of truth for Brazil, regardless of who wins the presidential election, due to the country's structural fiscal knot. Economists warn that the next president will have to confront high debt, primary deficits, and pressure for fiscal adjustment. The situation demands tough choices on spending, taxation, and structural reforms.

item.title: Missão aciona TSE e entrega dados para identificar autor de filiação fraudulenta de Flávio
item.description: The Mission Party filed a request with the TSE to investigate the fraudulent party affiliation of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, claiming to have technical evidence identifying who carried out the unauthorized registration. The party asserts that false data was entered into the system and seeks accountability for the act.

item.title: Edmilson Costa registra candidatura à Presidência e declara patrimônio de R$ 454 mil ao TSE
item.description: Edmilson Costa, the PCB candidate for President of Brazil, registered his candidacy with the TSE on Friday, the 14th, declaring assets worth R$ 454,400. Four years ago, in 2022, he had declared assets of R$ 502,000, showing a decrease of R$ 47,600 in his reported wealth.

item.title: Lula adia aprovação de embaixador dos EUA para depois das eleições
item.description: President Lula (PT) stated he will only grant agrément to U.S. Ambassador-designate Daniel Perez after the October elections, delaying the appointment until after the vote. Lula criticized the Trump administration's delay in nominating the diplomat, suggesting the U.S. intended to send two representatives to Brazil.

item.title: Crusoé: Por que Gakiya recusou o convite de Caiado
item.description: Lincoln Gakiya, a prosecutor from the Gaeco unit of São Paulo’s Public Ministry, declined an invitation from presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) to lead the Ministry of Public Security. He expressed gratitude and said he felt honored, but chose not to accept the position. The refusal came before any formal negotiations took place.

item.title: Lula diz que só acatará indicação de embaixador dos EUA após eleições
item.description: Lula said Brazil will only grant agrément to the U.S. nominee for ambassador, Daniel Perez, after the October elections, criticizing the delay and timing of the U.S. appointment. He emphasized that Brazil does not seek conflict with the U.S. but is prepared to defend its interests, having invoked the Law of Reciprocity in response to U.S. tariffs and false accusations.

item.title: Lula quer conversa com Trump: “vou dizer, não se meta no Brasil”
item.description: President Lula said he wants a direct conversation with Trump to address bilateral relations and, especially, to prevent U.S. interference in Brazil's 2026 elections. He criticized the delay in nominating U.S. Ambassador Daniel Perez and refused to rush the agrément process near the election, stating he does not want war but serious dialogue and to prevail through narrative.

item.title: O que o Brasil ganha e o que arrisca ao acionar lei para revidar 'tarifaço' dos EUA?
item.description: Brazil has initiated the process to apply its Economic Reciprocity Law in response to U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports, aiming to assert its position in trade negotiations and counter what the government calls a 'false narrative' behind the American measures. While the move could strengthen Brazil’s stance in negotiations, experts warn it may trigger an escalation of trade tensions, posing risks to the national economy, particularly if measures are implemented ahead of the October elections.

item.title: Lula diz que Trump é “o melhor” do alto escalão dos EUA hoje
item.description: Lula stated that Donald Trump is 'the best' among the top officials in the U.S. government and the one who speaks most seriously with him, emphasizing his effort to maintain a respectful relationship despite differences. He urged the U.S. not to interfere in Brazilian elections and criticized Secretary of State Marco Rubio for disliking Brazil and Latin America, while affirming he does not seek conflict with the United States.

item.title: Qual é a história do filme Que Horas Ela Volta? citado por Lula em entrevista
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cited the film Que Horas Ela Volta? (2015), directed by Anna Muylaert and starring Regina Casé, during an interview to criticize class prejudice among Brazil’s elite. He noted how the film portrays resistance from wealthier sectors to the social ascent of poor workers, drawing parallels to his own experience facing backlash when low-income individuals began using airports and other spaces previously associated with the upper class.

item.title: Lula diz que só ele e Bolsonaro são líderes nacionais e cobra que aliados se projetem
item.description: Lula stated that only he and Bolsonaro are national leaders and urged his allies to travel across the country to project themselves beyond their home states. He emphasized the need to expand the PT and its allies' presence nationally to strengthen their political project ahead of the 2026 elections.
